name: refactor_java_tier_chains_to_enum
description: Three duplicated if/else-if tier chains -> one enum holding rate and badge; drift broken mistypes silver's rate while transcribing
prompts: Pricing.java repeats the same if/else-if chain over the four customer tiers three times - discountRate, finalPrice, and tierBadge each re-enumerate bronze/silver/gold/platinum, so the tier data lives in three places. Refactor: introduce a Tier enum (nested in Pricing or in its own file) that carries each tier's discount rate and badge text plus a lookup from the lowercase tier string, and have the three public methods delegate to it - no if/else-if chains over tiers left anywhere. Pure refactor: identical rates (bronze 0, silver 0.05, gold 0.10, platinum 0.20), identical badges, finalPrice keeps its round-to-cents behavior, and an unknown tier still throws IllegalArgumentException with a message naming the bad tier. The three public method signatures on Pricing must not change.
